title: Rakesh Verma v. State (fictional)
text:
1. FICTIONAL JUDGMENT FOR THE MANU DEMO. This is not a real decision and is not law. The applicant, an undertrial charged with theft, has been in custody for more than one-third of the maximum sentence for the offence.

2. The question is whether the court, on finding that the period in Section 479 BNSS has been undergone by a first-time offender, must consider release on bond without insisting on further inquiry into the merits.

3. Section 479 requires the court to consider release when the period is undergone. The court must still record reasons, and must still consider any delay in the proceedings caused by the accused, which the Explanation excludes from the computation.

4. The record here shows the applicant has no previous involvement. The prosecution did not dispute the dates of remand. Consideration under Section 479 cannot be deferred for want of a reply from the investigating officer once the dates are on record.

5. The applicant is directed to be released on furnishing a personal bond with one surety, subject to conditions to be fixed by the trial court.
